source.title: On the Origin of Implicit Regularization in Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Samuel L. Smith; Benoit Dherin; D. G. Barrett; Soham De

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training experiments that refine the role of finite learning rates and regularization. Its results bear on V1’s training-error qualification, while most of its experiments address generalization rather than the listed training-error claim.
record.gate_note: Most reported outcomes concern test accuracy or loss and do not measure the claim’s near-zero training classification-error outcome. Training accuracy is reported in appendix C for Wide-ResNet CIFAR-10 and appendix D for Fashion-MNIST; only those relevant results are extracted. The paper’s cited claims about other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports CIFAR-10 convolutional-network training accuracy under different learning rates and explicit regularization strengths, bearing on V1's regularized-recipe qualification. Its generalization results and discussion of catapult dynamics do not test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive a first-order modified-loss description of mean random-shuffling SGD dynamics for small finite learning rates and empirically show that its explicit regularizer can improve test accuracy. They suggest it explains some large-learning-rate training plateaus, while acknowledging finite compute, higher-order corrections, and failure of their analysis near instability.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies the implicit regularization and generalization effects of finite-learning-rate SGD, not a systematic sweep of model size or training error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. It reports CIFAR-10 training-accuracy behavior for a Wide-ResNet and a separate 100% training-accuracy result on Fashion-MNIST.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes CIFAR-10 training-accuracy behavior: smaller rates had not converged within 6400 epochs and larger rates plateaued. On Fashion-MNIST, the authors report 100% training accuracy if the learning rate is not too large.

fits_no_version.finding: The Fashion-MNIST ReLU MLP consistently achieves 100% training accuracy when the learning rate is not too large.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A highly overparameterized fully connected ReLU network trained with SGD can interpolate Fashion-MNIST at suitable learning rates.

record.problems: For the CIFAR-10 Wide-ResNet training-accuracy result, the text provides qualitative descriptions rather than numeric values in the supplied figure text, and notes that the models may not have fully converged within the finite compute budget. The Fashion-MNIST result does not test V1’s specified CIFAR benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported training-error rows meet the claim-relatedness criteria. Test-accuracy results, test-loss results, and cited prior-work results are outside the measured behavior required by the versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR training error cannot be established from the supplied accuracy values. CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and controlled model-size or early-stopping comparisons are untested.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Depth degradation and matched comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth.
Recovery above an initial stability threshold, curvature trajectories, and edge-of-stability training. Catapult dynamics are discussed through prior work.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization or Fixup.

missing.what: Separate training-accuracy conditions for the modified loss: small regularization coefficients permit high training accuracy, while large coefficients prevent high training accuracy. The latter is explicit qualitative evidence for V1's regularized-recipe qualification; exact percentages are unavailable.
missing.locator: Appendix C, Figure 5(a) caption; Section 2.3 for the training recipe

record.verdict_notes: R1 alone warrants no near-zero-error verdict: an optimal learning rate and a training plateau do not establish the magnitude of training error. The supplied text contains no readable numerical accuracy curves.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, Adam, smaller-model comparison, early-stopping comparison, or substantial training-error result for the CIFAR-10 Wide-ResNet is reported.

rows.subject: 10-1 Wide-ResNet
rows.stage_stated: trained from initialization; initialization type not stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the original loss C(ω) at a range of learning rates; appendix C reports training accuracy within 6400 epochs.
rows.value: Figure 5(a) says training accuracy within 6400 epochs is maximized when learning rate ϵ = 2−9; smaller rates have not yet converged and larger rates reach a plateau.
rows.note: The text characterizes the curve but gives no training-accuracy percentage; it does not establish whether error is near zero.
rows.check: The supplied figure text gives no accuracy magnitude establishing near-zero or substantial training error. Initialization is stated: SkipInit, without batch normalization. The recipe also includes data augmentation and L2 weight decay of 5×10^-4.

rows.subject: fully connected MLP
rows.size_stated: 3 nonlinear layers, each width 4096, plus a final linear softmax layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with vanilla SGD; the authors report training accuracy when the learning rate is not too large.
rows.note: Fashion-MNIST is outside V1’s named CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 benchmark scope. The model is described as highly over-parameterized.
rows.check: The reported 100% training accuracy is accurate, but a fully connected Fashion-MNIST model does not measure V1's convolutional-network result on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100. Its observed state cannot be transferred to V1.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, 10-1 Wide-ResNet, strong explicit gradient-norm regularization, learning rate 2^-9, 6400 epochs
relationships.reason: Figure 5(a) explicitly reports failure to achieve high training accuracy at large regularization coefficients, supporting V1's regularized-recipe qualification. This verdict uses text omitted from R1; the required row is listed in missing.
relationships.display_finding: Large regularization coefficients prevented high training accuracy even after 6,400 epochs.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
